findings.issue: Four of the row's nine folded candidates -- 'positional identity' -> L4, 'silent resource downgrade' -> L6, 'reuse-detector matching semantics' -> L11, and 'multilingual leakage' -> L10 -- have no anchor an independent reviewer can open and check. They do not appear in docs/PROPOSED_lessons_L14_L23...md (read in full; none of the 10 proposed lessons use these terms), and the row's only anchor for them is a blanket citation to 'four reader reports over posed CHANGELOG 1.31-1.63' with no release number, section, or artifact path. I traced the labels to the external Codex review document (EDU_SKILL_CREATOR_CR_1.10_CODEX_REVIEW_2026-07-28.md, Disposition Table), which approves folding them using the same bare labels and cites no underlying evidence of its own either -- so the labels have been carried forward through two documents without ever being grounded in an inspectable artifact. Approving this row as-is would let four unverifiable claims become permanent doctrine in lessons_learned.md, which is exactly the failure mode the independent-review stage exists to catch.
findings.fix: Before the gate opens, either (a) attach a specific CHANGELOG release/section or reader-report excerpt for each of the four items so a reviewer can open and confirm them, or (b) move them to the 'declined' list (or a new 'insufficiently evidenced' bucket) pending better sourcing, leaving only the five traceable folds (L15, L17, L21, L22, and the L19/L20 folds already covered by f6) in this row.
findings.resolution: Split: f8 now carries only the four folds traceable to the L14-L23 document; the four changelog-sourced folds moved to a new f18, each anchored to a named release (1.58.1, 1.63.1, 1.41.1, 1.37, 1.37.1) verified directly in POSED @2ca8f7b before re-assertion.

findings.issue: The finding states the 128-byte forged 'passed' report (posed 1.38) was 'cited by a human approval,' but the CHANGELOG text says it was cited by a '5h approve' -- posed-instructional-designer, a fresh-context AI reviewer role, not a human/faculty gate. This inflates an AI-fooled-by-AI incident into a human-fooled-by-a-forged-report incident, which is a materially different (and more alarming) claim than the evidence supports.
findings.fix: Correct the clause to 'cited by an AI reviewer's (5h) approval' or similar. The row's broader L11 corollary about self-interested verification reports still holds without this specific overstatement -- the 1.34 anchor (15 hand-written gate decisions) is a genuine human-gate forgery case and can carry that part of the argument.
findings.resolution: f3 finding text corrected: the forged report was cited by an AI reviewer's approval (the 5h instructional-designer role), not a human gate. The human-gate forgery case is carried by the separate 1.34 anchor, which the review confirmed exact.

findings.issue: The row bundles nine independent fold-decisions (each landing in a different existing lesson: L1, L4, L6, L7, L9, L10, L11 x multiple) plus a tenth deferred item, all under one approve/defer/reject decision. If the faculty agrees with five folds but doubts one (plausibly the four flagged blocking above), the per-row gate forces an all-or-nothing call on all nine. This is the exact 'big gates overload the human' problem lessons_learned.md's own L4 names, and f6 in this same ledger was explicitly split for a smaller version of the same reason.
findings.fix: Split f8 into at least two rows: one for the folds traceable to the L14-L23 document (L15, L17, L21, L22 -- these check out and can be approved together with reasonable confidence), and one for the four untraceable items pending the evidence fix above. A per-destination-lesson split would be even cleaner if the faculty wants finer control.
findings.resolution: f8 split into f8 and f18 (see finding 1), so the faculty decides the two provenance groups separately rather than nine destinations at once.

note: This ledger is materially stronger than a typical first pass: of roughly twenty specific, checkable claims spot-checked directly against POSED's CHANGELOG.md at 2ca8f7b and the edu-skill-creator repo at ea1a9ce (including several exact verbatim quotes reproduced letter-for-letter, and one precise numeric census of stage-end summaries that matched exactly), all but a handful confirmed cleanly, and the three prior corrections the drafter flagged itself (f5, f7, f11 no longer smuggling POSED's hash-ledger, locked-graph, or registry-fix as universal doctrine) held up under scrutiny -- the mechanism-versus-capability discipline this ledger exists to enforce is genuinely being applied, not just claimed. The gate should not open uniformly yet, however: f3 overstates an AI-reviewer-fooled-by-forgery incident as a human-gate failure, and f8 both bundles nine unrelated fold-decisions into one all-or-nothing row and, within that bundle, carries four specific claims (positional identity, silent resource downgrade, reuse-detector matching semantics, multilingual leakage) that trace back only to an ephemeral 'four reader reports' handle with no artifact either I or the ledger's own upstream Codex review could actually open and check -- exactly the kind of ungrounded assertion an independent review is supposed to catch before it becomes permanent doctrine. Fix f3's wording, split and re-source f8, and the remaining fifteen rows are in good enough shape for the faculty's per-row gate as written, with the minor items noted for optional cleanup.
